name: palladium.ability.argon.dome
description: When enabled, creates a dome of air around the user's position. For its duration, the user, their team, and their pets inside it take less physical damage, and projectiles from anyone else bounce off its surface. Hostile mobs inside it are pushed back out.

fields.description: The radius of the dome in blocks.
How long the dome lasts.
The fraction from 0 to 1 of melee and projectile damage removed for those protected inside.
Whether projectiles that are not from the user's allies bounce off the dome.
Whether every player inside is protected instead of only the user's team.
How hard hostile mobs inside the dome are pushed out each tick. 0 disables it.

name: Sensory Overload
description: While enabled, overwhelms the wearer's senses: a visual-only warp, lagging camera, screen shake, activation flash, pulsing tint and muffled non-music sound.

fields.description: How strong the nausea-style screen warp is, from 0 (none) to 2 (well beyond the vanilla effect's own strength); reproduces the vanilla visual directly rather than applying the real Nausea effect.
How sluggishly the rendered view drags behind the wearer's actual look direction, from 0 (none) to 1 (heavy drag).
The weakest a single camera-shake pulse can be.
The strongest a single camera-shake pulse can be.
Whether a brief full-screen flash plays on activation.
The color of the activation flash, when flash_enabled is true.
How many ticks the activation flash takes to fade from full brightness to nothing.
The color of the full-screen tint that pulses while enabled.
The pulsing tint's peak opacity at the brightest point of each pulse.
How many pulses per second the full-screen tint cycles through.
Volume multiplier applied to non-music sounds while enabled, from 0 (silent) to 1 (unchanged).

name: Attribute Modifier
description: Adds an attribute modifier to the entity while the ability is enabled.

fields.description: The attribute modifier(s) that will be applied

name: Name Change
description: Changes the name of the player executing the ability.

fields.description: The new name of the player.

name: Blink
description: On activation, teleports you up to "distance" blocks along your look direction, stopping before solid blocks and optionally passing through non-opaque ones like glass ("allow_see_through").

fields.description: The maximum distance, in blocks, the user is teleported.
Whether transparent-but-solid blocks (glass, etc.) are passed through rather than stopping the teleport early.

fields.type: List of Particle Effects (particle*, count, spread, speed, offset)
fields.description: Optional particle effects played at the user's start and end positions in list order, skipped if the user doesn't actually move, where each entry is a full particle options object with an optional world-space offset.

name: Teleport
description: Teleports the entity to where it is looking as soon as the ability gets enabled. If it looks at a block, it lands right in front of or on top of it. If it looks into the air, it ends up as far as the range allows. If there isn't enough room at the destination, nothing happens.

fields.description: How many blocks the entity can teleport at most.
If true, the entity only teleports when it looks at a block within range. Otherwise it teleports into the air at the end of the range.
Action(s) that are performed after every teleport, at the new position.

name: Force Start Flight
description: On activation, immediately starts flying instead of waiting for the double-jump/fly-key gesture, but only while a palladium:flight ability is already enabled.

name: Multiversal Variant Swap
description: While enabled, shows an icon near the hotbar for the item in "slot" and lets the mouse wheel cycle it through its available multiversal variants without touching any other item data.

fields.description: The equipment or Curios slot whose item's variant gets cycled.
Pixel offset applied to the icon/label's on-screen position relative to its default placement above the hotbar.
If true, scrolling reversibly swaps in the variant's actual physical item instead of just changing the variant component, carrying over the stack's other components.

name: Fluid Transfer (All)
description: When enabled, moves as much of the fluid as fits from the fluid item in "from_slot" to the one in "to_slot" at once. What doesn't fit stays in the source.

fields.description: Which slot to take the fluid-storing item to draw from.
Which slot to take the fluid-storing item to fill.
The fluid that must be stored on both the "from_slot" and "to_slot" items for the transfer to happen.

name: Web Walking
description: While enabled, the user walks through cobwebs without being slowed down.

name: Random Effect
description: While enabled, periodically grants the user one randomly-chosen status effect from a list, rolling independently every "interval" ticks so the same effect can repeat.

fields.type: List of Effect Entries (effect, duration, amplifier*, particles*, show_icon*)
fields.description: The pool of effects to randomly choose from, each entry giving an effect, duration, and optional amplifier, particles, and show_icon.
How long to wait between rolls.

name: Dummy
description: A dummy ability that does nothing.

name: palladium.ability.argon.vortex
description: When enabled, creates a vortex of cutting air where the user is looking, on the ground at the end of the aim. For its duration it pulls living entities inside it towards its centre and damages them in pulses.

fields.description: How far away, in blocks, the vortex can be placed.
The radius of the vortex in blocks.
How long the vortex lasts.
Damage dealt per second to each entity inside. 0 for a vortex that does no damage.
The most damage the vortex deals to one entity in total.
How strongly entities are pulled towards the centre each tick.
How often damage is dealt.
Damage type ID the damage is dealt as. Unset, it is a player attack for players and a mob attack otherwise.
Whether the vortex forms around the living entity the user is looking at within max_distance and follows it for its duration, instead of forming on the ground.
Whether the vortex forms around the user and follows them instead of where they are aiming.
For this long after forming, entities small enough hover in the air inside the vortex instead of falling. 0 for none.
The largest bounding box volume, in cubic blocks, of an entity that gets suspended. A zombie is about 0.7 and an iron golem about 5. Bosses are never suspended.
Whether a layered swirling funnel of wind is drawn over the vortex.

name: Damage Reduction
description: While enabled, multiplies incoming damage (optionally limited to the given damage_types) by a percentage of its original value, where 0 blocks all damage and 100 leaves it unchanged.

fields.description: The percentage of the original damage the entity ends up taking, e.g. 0 for none or 150 for 50% more.
Optional damage types (or tags) the percentage is limited to, otherwise it applies to all incoming damage.

name: Gui Overlay
description: Renders an image on the screen.

fields.description: The texture to render.
The width of the texture.
The height of the texture.
The translation of the texture.
The rotation of the texture.
The scale of the texture.
Determines how the image is aligned on the screen.
If enabled, the image is hidden together with the rest of the GUI when pressing F1. Disable it for images that should always stay visible, like the inside of a helmet.

name: Screen Shake
description: While enabled, shakes the ability holder's camera only, with each pulse randomly varying in intensity between base_intensity and max_intensity for an uneven tremor feel.

fields.description: The weakest a single shake pulse can be.
The strongest a single shake pulse can be.

name: Damage Field
description: While enabled, continuously deals damage, as a given damage type, to every living entity touching the entity's own hitbox (optionally inflated).

fields.description: How much to inflate the entity's hitbox, in blocks, when checking for entities to affect, where 0 uses its exact hitbox.
The amount of damage dealt each tick to entities touching the field, plus the user's attack damage attribute if apply_user_damage is true.
The damage type the damage is dealt as.
If true, adds the user's current attack damage attribute (including equipment and effect modifiers) on top of "damage" each tick.

name: Prevent Death
description: Prevents the entity from dying. When it would die, it keeps a bit of health instead, similar to a Totem of Undying. It takes effect before a totem would be used, so totems are not wasted while this ability is active.

fields.description: The health the entity is left with after its death was prevented. Can't be higher than its max health.
If true, all effects are removed from the entity when its death is prevented, like a totem does. This also stops effects like poison or wither from finishing the entity off right away.
Damage types that still kill the entity. Defaults to the #minecraft:bypasses_invulnerability tag, which covers things like the void and /kill.
Action(s) that are performed every time a death is prevented.

name: Sound
description: Plays a sound.

fields.description: The sound that is being played.
The volume for the played sound.
The pitch for the played sound.
Whether or not the sound should loop during the time the ability is enabled.
Whether or not the sound should be played to just the player executing the ability, or to all players.

name: Breath
description: While enabled, scales the entity's maximum breath and how fast it refills out of water, as percentages of vanilla. Multiple active Breath abilities stack multiplicatively.

fields.description: The entity's max breath as a percentage of the vanilla default (300 ticks), e.g. 100 for unchanged or 200 for double.
How fast the breath refills out of water, as a percentage of vanilla's speed: 100 is unchanged, 200 twice as fast. Independent of "percentage" and stacks multiplicatively with other Breath abilities.

name: Carry
description: While enabled, pressing the ability's key grabs the first living entity hit by a forward raycast, holding it until the key is pressed again (drop) or, if throwable, the player right-clicks (throw).

fields.description: How far forward the grab raycast reaches.
How many blocks in front of the player the carried target is held. Defaults to 2.0.
Extra vertical offset applied to the carried target's held position. Defaults to 0.0.
If true, right-clicking while carrying throws the target instead of requiring the key to drop it. Defaults to false.
Velocity applied to the target when thrown, in the player's look direction. Only relevant if throwable is true. Defaults to 1.5.

name: Power Transfer
description: On activation, opens a GUI for transferring superpower-granted powers between the user and a nearby entity targeted by the crosshair.

fields.description: Maximum crosshair distance to a living entity for it to become the transfer target.

name: Structure Capture
description: While held, drag out and scroll-resize a wireframe cuboid (up to "max_size" per axis); on release, captures and clears its blocks into a capsule item that restores them, rotated to match, on right-click.

fields.description: The maximum distance, in blocks, the look-target raycast can reach.
The maximum size of the captured area along each axis, measured from the block first looked at.
The outline color, defaulting to cyan when unset.

name: Teleport to Location
description: On activation, teleports the entity to the position, facing and dimension saved under "namespace" by argon:save_location, searching up for open space, or does nothing if none is saved.

fields.description: The name of the location to teleport to, as previously saved by an argon:save_location ability using the same namespace.

Reference to another ability, e.g. "fsang:example#driving_ability", to cut short once the teleport happens, so a later step in a shared animation-timer sequence doesn't fire after the entity's state changes.

name: Teleportation (Menu)
description: On activation, opens a client-side GUI to teleport by coordinates, saved locations, or both depending on "mode", opening a portal instead of an instant teleport when create_portal is true.

fields.description: Whether the coordinate section includes a dimension selector, otherwise the destination is always the user's current dimension.
Dimension IDs to hide from the dimension selector when show_dimensions is true.
Which teleport method(s) the menu offers: coordinates (default), saved_locations, or both.
How many saved-location slots to offer when mode is saved_locations or both.
If true, opens a pair of linked, reusable portals instead of teleporting instantly, using "portal"'s settings instead of "direct_teleport"'s.

fields.type: Portal Settings (beam_renderer, beam_vector, duration, thickness, distance, particles)
fields.description: Portal visuals and behavior used when create_portal is true, with distance measured via raycast from the user (0 = at the user).

fields.type: Direct Teleport Settings (entity_range, origin_particles, destination_particles, origin_beam, destination_beam)
fields.description: Settings used when create_portal is false, including how far nearby entities are brought along and one-time particle/beam effects at the departure and arrival points.

name: Item Database (Create)
description: On activation, opens a searchable list of everything in the user's item database - clicking an entry gives the user 1 more copy of it.

fields.description: Whether created items are exact duplicates of what was stored (enchantments, damage, name, etc.), or plain default copies of the item type when false.
Maximum number of items each database entry can create before it must be re-stored to reset its count, unlimited if unset.

name: Command
description: An ability that executes commands.

fields.description: The commands that are executed during each tick of the ability being active.
The commands that are executed upon activating the ability.
The commands that are executed on the last tick of the ability being active.

name: palladium.ability.argon.melee_armor_penetration
description: While enabled, the user's direct melee hits ignore part of the target's armor. Hits dealt by argon:energy_beam and argon:held_target use their own armor_penetration instead.

fields.description: The fraction from 0 to 1 of the damage armor would have absorbed that is ignored.

name: Taunt
description: While enabled, forces every mob within range to target the user.

fields.description: How far from the entity other mobs can be to be forced to target it.

name: Restrict Slots
description: Restricts the slots of the entity.

fields.description: The slots that should be restricted.

name: Prevent Effects
description: Prevents the entity from being able to gain OR only be able to gain the specified effects. Does NOT clear effects.

fields.description: If to be immune to all BUT the specified effects.
The effects that you will be immune to.

name: Flight
description: Allows the player to fly using a pre-defined flight type

fields.description: The ID of the flight type that will be used.
Multiplier applied to the speeds defined in the flight type.

name: Gliding
description: Allows the player to use the elytra gliding

name: Wall Crawl
description: While enabled, claims idle appendages to reach for nearby surfaces. While enough keep hold, you get free flight-style movement (no gravity); with too few, normal gravity returns.

fields.description: How far, in blocks, each appendage searches for a surface, and the maximum stretch before it releases and re-searches.
How many appendages must stay attached for flight to remain active; below this, gravity/normal physics resume immediately.
How many appendages this ability claims and uses at once.
How quickly velocity catches up to the target each tick while flying (0-1); higher feels snappier, lower feels floatier.
Horizontal WASD-driven flight speed while climbing.
Vertical speed while holding jump (up) or shift (down) while climbing.

name: Sculk Immunity
description: When enabled, the player will not cause any walk-related sculk vibrations anymore.

name: Slide
description: While enabled, pressing crouch during a sprint launches the entity into a ground slide along its facing direction, knocking back any living entities it slides into.

fields.description: Horizontal blocks/tick the slide starts at.
How many ticks the slide lasts (speed decays linearly to 0 over this time).
Per-tick retention (0-1) of any pre-existing horizontal velocity blended into the slide. Defaults to 0.93.
Knockback strength applied to entities the slide sweeps into, in the slide's direction.
How far past the entity's own hitbox the knockback sweep reaches each tick. Defaults to 1.0.

name: Chat Color
description: While enabled, recolors every chat message the user sends to a fixed color, applied to the whole message uniformly.

fields.description: The color to apply to the user's chat text, as a hex string (e.g. "#FF0000") or a named color (e.g. "red").

name: Skin Change
description: An ability that changes the player's skin.

fields.description: The texture that should be used for the player's skin.
Model type for the player. If left empty it will keep the player's model type. 'wide' = Wide-armed Steve model; 'slim' = Slim-armed Alex model;
Priority for the skin (in case multiple skin changes are applied, the one with the highest priority will be used)

name: Invisibility
description: Makes the player invisible. Also makes mobs not see the player anymore.

fields.description: The opacity the player will adapt
The opacity at which the player will see themself. If this is being set to something less than 0 it will use the default opacity setting.
A multiplier for how visible the player is to mobs. 0.0 means completely invisible, 1.0 means normal visibility.

name: Drown
description: Forces each configured target, the user or every entity within range, to drain their oxygen bar as if drowning.

fields.description: Who this ability forces to drown, each entry either {"type": "self"} or {"type": "range", "range": <value>}. A single entry may be given without the list, and an entry with no range may be just its type ("self").

How fast targets' breath drains, as a percentage of vanilla's drowning speed: 100 is unchanged, 200 twice as fast. The highest value wins if several Drown abilities target one entity. Match argon:breath's "percentage" to keep the vanilla time with a bigger breath.

Whether bubbles rise round the head of each target while they are drowned. Set it to false for a drain that should not show. If several Drown abilities target the same entity, the bubbles show if any of them has this on.

name: Blast Chain
description: Fires a beam that deals damage only on reaching its target, then, if it hit a living entity, fires on to the nearest other visible living entity, up to "chain_count" more times.

fields.description: The id of the beam renderer to use for every segment of the chain.
The damage dealt to the entity hit by the initial shot.

Multiplier applied to "damage" for each chain jump already taken (e.g. 0.85 means the 2nd hit deals 85% damage, the 3rd 72.25%, etc). Leave at 1 for no falloff. Effects always apply at their configured strength regardless of this value.
The maximum distance the initial shot can travel before giving up.
The blocks every beam piece (initial shot and every chain jump) travels per tick.
The length of the traveling beam piece, in blocks.
How many ticks each hit entity is set on fire for.
If the initial shot should ignite flammable blocks it hits instead of a living entity.
If the initial shot should smelt the block it hits instead of a living entity.
The maximum number of additional jumps after the initial hit.
How far, in blocks, from each impact point to search for the next chain target.
Whether a chain jump is allowed to pick the caster as its next target. The initial shot never hits the caster regardless of this setting.

Applied, at full configured strength, to every entity hit by the chain (the initial hit and every jump). Same entry format as "potion_hit"'s "effects": effect, duration, amplifier*, max_amplifier* and particles*.

The damage type the damage is dealt as, a damage type ID such as "minecraft:magic" or one added by a pack. Left unset, the damage is exactly what it always was: a player attack when a player uses this and a mob attack otherwise. If the damage type does not exist, that default is used.

name: palladium.ability.argon.silence
description: While enabled, the user makes no sounds, such as footsteps and other movement sounds. It does not make the user invisible or hide their vibrations from sculk sensors (use palladium:sculk_immunity for that).

name: Armor Slots (Store)
description: Stores the items in the given slots under an ID and empties those slots, to be restored later with a matching restore_equipment ability.

fields.description: The ID the stored items are saved under.
The slots whose items should be stored and cleared.

name: Drown
description: Makes the target lose air as if it was underwater, so it starts drowning once the air runs out. Respiration still slows it down, players in creative mode are not affected.

fields.description: Who is drowned. "self" drowns the entity with the ability, "looked_at" drowns the living entity it looks at within the range. That entity stays the target until the ability is disabled or the target dies.
How far away the looked at entity can be, in blocks. Only used for "looked_at".
How fast the target loses air as a percentage of normal drowning. 200 drowns it twice as fast. If several Drown abilities hit the same target, the highest value is used.
Whether bubbles rise around the head of the target.

name: Untargetable
description: While enabled, keeps hostile mobs from targeting the user, either entirely or narrowed by "mobs" and "mode" ("whitelist" only those mobs, "blacklist" every mob except those).

fields.description: How "mobs" is interpreted: "whitelist" (only these can't target the user) or "blacklist" (everything except these can't target the user). Irrelevant while "mobs" is unset.
The mob type(s) this applies to, as explicit entity type IDs, a tag ("#namespace:tag"), or a mix of both. Left unset, this ability applies to every hostile mob.

name: Immunity
description: While enabled, blocks the listed status effects from being applied to the user, optionally up to a maximum level per effect, and removes any matching effects they already have.

fields.type: List of Immune Effect Entries (effect, level*)
fields.description: List of effects to block, each with an "effect" id and an optional "level" (amplifier cap) below which immunity applies, or all levels if unset.

name: Multi-Jump
description: While enabled, lets the entity perform extra mid-air jumps, up to a set number, until it touches the ground and refills them.

fields.description: How many extra mid-air jumps the entity can perform before landing again.
The vertical velocity applied per extra jump, defaulting to a normal jump's strength.

name: Color Cycle Glow
description: While enabled, gives the entity a see-through-walls outline that cycles through "colors" in order, in sync for everyone since it follows world time. Independent of entity_glow and the Glowing effect.

fields.description: The ordered list of colors to cycle through and fade between; must contain at least one color.
How many ticks (20 per second) each fade from one color to the next takes.

name: Movement Reduction
description: While enabled, reduces the entity's ground movement or flight speed by a percentage, optionally reducing its attack damage by the same amount.

fields.description: Whether to reduce ground movement speed ("movement") or flight speed ("flight").
The percentage to reduce the chosen speed by, from 0 (no effect) to 100 (fully stopped).
If true, also reduces the entity's attack damage by the same percentage.

name: Healing
description: An ability that heals the entity every x ticks by y amount.

fields.description: The frequency of healing (in ticks)
The amount of hearts for each healing

name: Zoom
description: While enabled, zooms your view to the magnification given by "zoom" and eases back out when disabled. It follows "zoom" as it changes, so a data attachment can let scrolling adjust it. Only affects your own view.

fields.description: The magnification to zoom to: 1 is normal, 2 shows things at twice the size, 4 at four times. A value, so it can follow a data attachment (e.g. an integer_data_attachment) to be changed while zoomed. Below 1 counts as 1, and 100 is the most. With "level_factor" above 1 it is a level instead (see there).
How quickly the view closes on the magnification, per second, when zooming and when "zoom" changes. Higher is snappier: 6 covers about 63% of the way in a sixth of a second.
1 (default) means "zoom" is the magnification. Above 1, "zoom" is a level and the magnification is level_factor raised to it, so every scroll step changes the view by the same proportion.
Whether turning the camera slows down as the view zooms in, so aiming stays steady (the same idea as a spyglass). At 4x, the camera turns a quarter as far for the same mouse movement.
Whether draw distances grow with the zoom so magnified things stay visible: block entities, other entities, sign outlines and name tags. Only already-loaded terrain can show.

Whether turning the zoom off puts the zoom level back to "base_level" (in "level_attachment"), so the next time it starts from the base again instead of from wherever it was scrolled to. Needs "level_attachment".
The number data attachment that holds the zoom level (the one "zoom" reads and scrolling changes), which "reset_on_disable" sets back to "base_level". Only used by "reset_on_disable".
The value "reset_on_disable" sets the level attachment to.

name: Energy Beam
description: Shoots a beam that can reflect off blocks and, on hitting a matching entity, either redirect onward or spread into several beams once, applying damage, fire, and smelting along its path.

fields.description: The id of the beam renderer to use.
Damage dealt to every entity the beam hits. A value, so it can follow a data attachment to scale with a level.
Total distance the beam can travel across all its bounces. A value, so it can follow a data attachment to scale with a level.
Maximum number of times the beam can reflect off blocks or entities (a spread event also counts as one bounce) before stopping at its next hit.
How many ticks the beam sets a hit entity on fire for.
Whether the beam ignites flammable blocks it touches.
Whether the beam smelts every block it touches.
Whether the beam reflects off blocks it hits instead of stopping there, leaving only 'entity_reaction' able to redirect it when false.
What happens when the beam hits an entity matching 'entity_bounce_condition': continue, redirect, or spread into multiple beams.
Optional condition restricting which hit entities can redirect or spread the beam, ignored when 'entity_reaction' is 'none' and defaulting to all entities otherwise.
Number of beams the spread effect bursts into when 'entity_reaction' is 'spread'.
Angle in degrees the spread beams fan out from the central reflected direction when 'entity_reaction' is 'spread'.

Makes damage, fire, smelting and block mode reach across a cone instead of a line. Widths in blocks at the eyes ("start_size", 0.1) and at "end_distance" (default "max_distance"); "rays" (1-128, default 24) finds blocks. Pair with the argon:cone renderer.
How hard the beam pushes living entities away from the caster. 1 is firm, 5 is a gale, 0 is none. Weakened by knockback resistance. A value, so it can follow a data attachment to scale with a level.
Whether "knockback" ignores the target's knockback resistance.

What the beam does to blocks it hits: "type" is "melt" or "freeze", with "time" (default 60 ticks), "auto_time", "speed_multiplier", "modifiers", "conversions" and "particle"; freeze adds "frozen_time", "slippery", "friction" and "snow_layers". See the examples.

fields.type: { min_time, max_time, fire_time, taper, grow, shots, shot_interval, ignore_hit_immunity, curve, damage, max_distance, knockback, effect_amplifier, effect_duration }
fields.description: Turns the beam into a charged shot: hold the ability to charge and release to fire. Releasing before "min_time" (default 10) fires nothing and the charge is full at "max_time" (default 40), eased by "curve" (linear, ease_in, ease_out, ease_in_out). The beam then shows for "fire_time" (default 8), and with a "taper" from 0 to 1 it appears at full length and narrows to nothing over that fraction of the end of that time instead of retracting, and "grow" (default 0.15) is the fraction of the start over which it widens from nothing to full size. "shots" (default 1) fires that many shots "shot_interval" ticks apart (default 4), each aimed where you look at that moment, and "ignore_hit_immunity" lets every shot damage the same target. Each of the other settings is a { min, max } range used for damage, range, knockback and the amplifier and duration of the entity effects, from no charge to full charge. See the charged beam example.
Whether the beam passes through every entity in its way and hits all of them, stopping only at a block or its max_distance.
With pierce, the most entities the beam passes through: it ends at the last one. 0 is no limit.

With pierce, how far in blocks the beam's reach extends sideways (width) and up and down (height) around the line, so a wide flat or tall thin slash can hit entities beside its path. Default 0.3 for both.
How far, in blocks, hit living entities are launched away from the caster (or from the impact point), instead of the "knockback" strength. Weakened by knockback resistance.
Upward launch speed added by "knockback_distance" (0.4 is roughly a block and a half).
Upward launch speed used instead of "lift" while the caster is not on the ground.
How far, in blocks, hit living entities are pulled sideways across the caster's look direction toward the aim line, on top of any knockback. Weakened by knockback resistance.
The fraction from 0 to 1 of a hit entity's armor ignored by the damage.
Adds "bonus" damage to hit entities whose armor value is at least "threshold".

Makes the beam burst where it ends: every living entity within "radius" blocks of that point is hit instead of the entities on the line, launched away from the point, with damage reduced by up to "falloff" (0 to 1) at the edge.

fields.type: List of { shape*, particle*, anchor, count, radius, step, pitch, strands, arc, height, rings, speed, spread }
fields.description: Particle effects spawned when the beam fires, for beams that should look like air or smoke instead of a laser. "shape" is "streak" (particles along the beam every "step" blocks with "spread" jitter), "helix" ("strands" spirals of "radius" and "pitch" along the beam), "ring" ("rings" rings up to "radius" with "count" particles each, only "arc" degrees facing forward if under 360), "sphere" ("count" particles on a sphere of "radius") or "burst" (the same, filled). "crescent" draws crescent-shaped arcs of "count" particles along the beam every "step" blocks, spanning "arc" degrees (150 by default), sideways or up and down by "orientation" ("horizontal" or "vertical"). "anchor" is "end" (where the beam ends, default) or "caster" for rings, "height" raises them, and "speed" sends the particles along the beam or outward.

fields.type: Array of { effect*, duration, amplifier, particles }
fields.description: Mob effects given to every living entity the beam hits. Duration is ticks or a time like "5s" (default 5s), amplifier 0 is level one, particles defaults to false.
Damage type ID the damage is dealt as. Unset, it is a player attack for players and a mob attack otherwise.
Damage types used instead of "damage_type" while their condition is true. Checked in order, first match wins. See the damage type overrides example.

name: Text Overlay
description: While enabled, renders text on screen using the same translate/rotate/scale/alignment transform as the built-in gui_overlay ability, but for text instead of an image.

fields.description: The text to render, either a plain string or a full text component (translate/keybind/color/etc).
A [x, y] pixel offset applied to the text's position.
The rotation of the text, in degrees.
The [x, y] scale of the text.
Determines how the text is aligned on the screen.
The color of the rendered text.
Whether the text has a drop shadow.

name: Forced Perspective
description: Locks the camera of the player into a perspective while enabled. The perspective the player had before is restored afterwards.

fields.description: The perspective the camera is locked into.

name: Aim
description: Allows the player to aim their arms.

fields.description: The arm(s) that should point.

name: Web Swing
description: On activation, attaches a rope anchor and swings you as a pendulum while enabled. The rope only cancels motion past its length, turning momentum into an arc. Movement keys steer; it ends on disable, or optionally on ground contact or lost line of sight.

fields.description: The maximum distance an anchor can attach to, measured from the eye to the exact hit point.

Which kind of raycast hit can be attached to: a fixed "block" anchor, a "entity" living entity that becomes a moving anchor followed for the rest of the swing, or "both" (whichever the raycast hits first).
The id of the beam renderer used to draw the rope from the user to the anchor point.

Extra rope length, in blocks, on top of the exact distance at the moment the web attaches. 0 (default) starts the rope exactly as long as the current distance, so attaching never snaps or stalls the user; raise it for a more dramatic catch.
Scales gravity's pull while swinging; 1 (default) is normal gravity. Other values compensate vanilla's own gravity rather than replacing it.

Acceleration, blocks/tick^2, from holding forward/back toward or away from where the user looks, projected onto the rope's tangent plane. It fades to nothing as speed approaches max_speed, and is off below a minimum speed so it can never hold the user hovering. 0 = purely momentum-driven.
Extra multiplier on velocity every tick while swinging, 0 to 1. 1 (default) keeps momentum (vanilla's own air drag is already undone, see drag_compensation).
Which hand the web comes from (drives left/right animation mirroring). Defaults to left if the beam_renderer id ends in "left", otherwise right.

Slowly takes slack out of the rope (never pulling the user, and never below their current distance plus rope_slack_tolerance), so a swing that goes slack gets a usable rope again instead of the web quietly failing.
How fast auto_tighten removes slack, blocks/tick.
Auto-tightening never shortens the rope below this length, blocks.
How much slack, blocks, auto_tighten leaves in the rope.
The most, in blocks per tick, the rope may move the user back onto its radius after an overshoot, so any correction is paid off gradually instead of as a snap.

Undo vanilla's per-tick air drag (x0.91 horizontal, x0.98 vertical) while swinging airborne, so a swing keeps its momentum instead of bleeding it into the air. Turn off only to compare against plain vanilla drag.
Caps the user's total speed, blocks/tick, while swinging. Defaults to 2.6; 0 removes the cap.

How far the rope has to sag, as a fraction of its own length, before the beam renders at maximum looseness. Only affects beam renderers (like argon:segmented_textured) that read this ability's rope tension for their sag, and only on the client that simulates the swing - everyone else sees a straight, taut web.

If present, holding jump reels the rope in and holding sneak reels it back out (up to the original attach length), both at "speed" blocks/tick, down to "min_length" blocks at the shortest. Leave unset (the default) to disable manual reeling.

Which conditions automatically detach the rope: "on_ground" when the user touches the ground, and "on_blocked_line" when a solid block ends up blocking the straight line between the user and the anchor point. Both default to true.

fields.type: Swing Assist Settings (anchor_cone_degrees*, min_anchor_distance*, anchor_height_weight*, velocity_blend_speed*, ground_clearance_strength*, lateral_steering_strength*, swing_jump_strength*, fall_damage_grace_ticks*, rope_wrap*)
fields.description: Targeting and assist tuning. Targeting is a direct raycast along the aim first (a valid hit always wins); only if that misses, or hits closer than "min_anchor_distance", a small cone of "anchor_cone_degrees" (default 10) is searched, with aim accuracy weighted far above "anchor_height_weight" (default 0.4, the most a high target can gain over an on-aim one). "velocity_blend_speed" (default 0 = off) blends the travel direction into the aim direction. "ground_clearance_strength" (default 0.5) softens downward speed just before grazing the ground. "lateral_steering_strength" (default 0.02) is the left/right equivalent of pump_acceleration. "swing_jump_strength" (default 0 = pure momentum release) is an optional boost applied if jump is held on release. "fall_damage_grace_ticks" (default 15) forgives fall damage for that long after release. "rope_wrap" (default true) lets the rope catch on the nearest obstruction between the anchor and the user.
fields.fallback: SwingAssistSettings[anchorConeDegrees=10.0, minAnchorDistance=3.0, anchorHeightWeight=0.4, velocityBlendSpeed=0.0, groundClearanceStrength=0.5, lateralSteeringStrength=0.02, swingJumpStrength=0.0, fallDamageGraceTicks=15, ropeWrap=true]

name: Equip Armor
description: On activation, equips each item into the matching slot by list index, overwriting whatever was worn there without storing it.

fields.description: The items to equip as plain item IDs (count always 1, no custom components), matched by order to 'slots'.
The slots to equip into, matched by order to 'items'.

name: Intangibility
description: Makes the entity intangible to certain blocks.

Block tag which includes the block the player can phase through. Leave null for all blocks.
Block tag which includes the block the player can phase through. Leave null for all blocks.

name: Projectile Effect
description: Shoots a projectile entity, identical to the built-in projectile ability, but can additionally grant one or more status effects to whatever living entity the projectile hits.

fields.description: ID of an entity type (must be a projectile).
Additional NBT data for the projectile entity.
Inaccuracy when shooting the projectile. A value, so it can change with conditions (for example a wider spread while overloaded).
Velocity with which the projectile is being shot.
The arm which will swing when the projectile is being shot.
Usually, the current velocity of player will be added to the projectile's velocity. This setting can disable that.
A [x, y, z] spawn offset, relative to the entity's facing direction. Defaults to [0, 0, 0].

Each entry configures its own effect, duration, amplifier*, particles*, and powers* (a list of {power, mode} entries, where "power" is an explicit power id, a power tag ("#namespace:tag"), or a mix of both - "include" requires a matching power, "exclude" forbids one) - all entries are granted to whatever living entity the projectile directly hits. Empty by default, meaning no effect is granted.

Only meaningful for an entity_type whose appearance includes an "item" appearance (e.g. "palladium:custom_projectile"). Tints every such appearance's item using whatever colour a registered source reads off an item in "slot" (a Palladium player slot, e.g. "mainhand", "curios:hands" - every item currently in that slot is checked, and the first one "source" finds a colour on wins), the same way a dyed item is tinted - so this only has a visible effect if the appearance item's own model has a tint-indexed layer to begin with. An id nothing has registered, or no matching item in the slot, silently leaves the appearance untinted; omit "item_tint" entirely for a projectile that should never be tinted.
If above 0, the projectile disappears once it has flown this many blocks from where it was shot.
If above 0, a living entity the projectile hits cannot sprint for this long.

name: Wall Crawling
description: Lets the user climb flat vertical walls and, optionally, ceilings using look-relative WASD, wrapping automatically around outside corners and rolling the camera so the attached surface reads as "down".

fields.description: The base crawling speed, in blocks per tick, before speed_multiplier is applied.
Multiplies base_speed - lets different powers reuse this same ability at different crawling speeds (0.5 = half speed, 2.0 = double) without a separate implementation.
How close to a wall or ceiling face the user must be to attach to (or remain attached to) it.
How hard jumping off a surface pushes the user in whichever direction they're currently looking.

A small constant velocity applied into the attached surface every tick, whether or not the user is moving - the same solid-block collision that stops it is what confirms the surface is still there, rather than a distance check.
Whether ceilings (not just vertical walls) are valid attachment surfaces.
If true, smoothly rolls the local user's own camera so the attached surface visually reads as "down" - the wall or ceiling becomes their floor, not just their movement plane.

Whether camera_roll also applies while the user is in third person, rather than only first person. Off by default since third person also shows the user's own model, which the roll does nothing to reorient.

If true, attaching to a surface turns the player's gravity toward it (the surface becomes their floor, with the hitbox, camera and model turning with it) instead of steering their velocity along it. Everything below applies to this mode.
A multiplier on normal gravity while attached; it is how firmly the player is held to the surface.
Whether the camera turns with the surface. If missing, camera_roll is used. When false the view stays upright to the world while the body and movement still turn.
Ticks the camera takes to turn to a new surface. 0 turns it at once.
Whether the camera and body turn gradually. When false every turn is instant.
Ticks the drawn body takes to turn to a new surface.
linear, ease_in, ease_out or ease_in_out: how the turns speed up and slow down.

What a turn between surfaces does to where the player is looking. relative: the same angles in the new gravity (looking level and forward stays level and forward across the new surface). world: the angles are recomputed so the player keeps looking at the same point in the world.
How close a surface must be to grab or keep hold of it, in blocks. If missing, attach_distance is used.
How far before the edge of a surface the player starts turning round it, in blocks (0 to 0.3).
surface_relative: W goes up the wall (or along the heading) whatever the camera does. camera_relative: W goes where the camera points, along the surface.
How hard jumping pushes the player straight off the surface. If missing, detach_strength is used.
Whether the player may turn onto surfaces where only a crawl-sized body fits, crawling through tight spaces.
Whether ceilings are valid surfaces. If missing, ceiling_crawling is used.
Whether the player turns automatically from one surface to the next at corners (and from the floor onto a wall they walk into). When false they can only grab a surface from the air.
Whether speed is kept through a turn between surfaces.
Multiplies the crawling speed (base_speed times speed_multiplier) on a surface only.
Whether sprinting makes the player crawl faster.

If true, the player is crawl-sized (the vanilla crawling pose, a 0.6 block hitbox that fits one-block gaps) on a wall or ceiling unless they are sprinting; sprinting stands them back up, as far as there is room.

Whether sprinting along a wall or ceiling plays the running animation. Vanilla only starts it from how far the player moves across the ground, which is nothing while climbing, so without this a sprinting crawler never runs. Only while sprinting; the ordinary crawl is unchanged.

name: Ground Beam
description: While enabled, draws damaging ground beams under entities with solid ground within "max_ground_depth" blocks. "mode" "area" (default) hits every other living entity within "range"; "target" only the one you look at.

fields.description: The id of the beam renderer to use for each ground-to-target beam.
In "area" mode, how far from the user, in blocks, to search for target entities. In "target" mode, the maximum distance, in blocks, the user can be looking at a target from.
Whether this affects every qualifying entity within "range" of the user ("area") or only the single qualifying entity the user is currently looking at ("target").
Maximum distance, in blocks, to search straight down from a target for solid ground. Targets with no ground found within this depth get no beam and take no damage that tick.
The damage dealt to every currently beamed entity every "damage_rate" ticks. Leave at 0 for a purely cosmetic beam.
How long, in ticks, to wait between damage applications.
If true, damaged entities are not knocked back.

Restricts which entities can be targeted based on the powers they hold. Each entry lists a "power" (an explicit power id, a power tag ("#namespace:tag"), or a mix of both) and an optional "mode" - "include" (default) requires at least one matching power to be present, "exclude" requires all of them to be absent; an entity only counts if it satisfies every entry. Leave unset (the default) to target all living entities in range.

The damage type the damage is dealt as, a damage type ID such as "minecraft:magic" or one added by a pack. Left unset, the damage is exactly what it always was: a player attack when a player uses this and a mob attack otherwise. If the damage type does not exist, that default is used.

name: Clone Remove
description: Dismisses some of the user's active clones. Doesn't refund the total clone limit.

fields.description: Which clones go first: oldest summoned, closest to the user, or furthest from the user.
How many clones to dismiss per activation.

description: Summons clones of the user that copy their look and gear and fight beside them. At max_active, activating dismisses the oldest clone instead.

fields.description: How many clones to summon per activation.
How many clones can exist at once.
Lifetime cap on clones summoned, ignoring dismissed ones. Unlimited if unset.

fields.type: List of Clone Modifiers (health*, attack_damage*, movement_speed*, powers*)
fields.description: Applied in order to every clone. Clones start with the user's max health, attack damage and movement speed. Each stat is a value (multiplier) or {"amount": value, "operation": "multiply" / "add" / "set"}. "powers" lists power ids to give the clone.

name: Grapple
description: Fires a grappling hook that flies out to a range and latches on contact: reels a hit living entity toward the caster, or reels the caster toward a hit block.

fields.description: The maximum distance the grapple can reach.
If true, the hook latches onto a living entity it flies into and reels it toward the caster. The entity's knockback resistance slows the reeling down, fully resistant entities can't be pulled.
If true, the hook latches onto a block it flies into and reels the caster toward it.
The velocity, in blocks/tick, that the pulled entity (or the caster) is reeled at.
The velocity, in blocks/tick, that the hook itself flies out at.
"held" keeps the grapple active only while the ability is enabled (released on disable); "one_shot" fires once and runs to completion on its own.
The id of the beam renderer used to draw the rope, e.g. one used by the swinging flight type or your own under assets/<namespace>/palladium/beams/.
Sound played once when the grapple is fired.
Looping sound played while the grapple is actively reeling.
Sound played once when the grapple detaches (arrives, times out, or is released mid-pull).

Action(s) that are performed during the last tick of the ability

name: Carry
description: While enabled, grabs the living entity you look at and holds it on a damped spring at an attachment point, so it lags and swings as you move but never strays past "maximum_distance". Disabling lets go.

fields.description: How far away, in blocks, a target can be grabbed from.

fields.type: [x, y, z] or a preset name
fields.description: Where the carried entity is drawn toward, in the wearer's frame (x right, y up from the feet, z forward): an [x, y, z] offset, or right_shoulder, left_shoulder, right_hand, left_hand, chest, above_head, or main/off_hand and main/off_shoulder by the wearer's main arm.
Radius around the attachment point inside which the target is held only loosely.
Radius around the attachment point the target can never leave (a wall can still push it past this).
Spring strength pulling the target to the attachment point.
How strongly the target's motion relative to the wearer is resisted - higher settles faster, lower swings longer.
How much of normal gravity acts on the target, so it hangs below the wearer when not being pulled up (0 = none, 1 = full).
The target's mass: spring and damping accelerations are divided by this, so higher means more lag and swing.
How much of each change in the wearer's velocity is passed straight on to the target (0 = only the spring moves it, 1 = it follows exactly).
Most ticks the initial pull-in lasts before normal carry physics takes over.
Whether the carried entity is kept out of walls: it is pulled back along the line from the wearer if a block is in the way, instead of being placed through it.
Whether the target keeps its velocity when let go, rather than stopping dead.
Whether non-player entities can be grabbed.
Whether players can be grabbed.
How strongly the carried entity pitches and rolls with the sway when drawn: 0 keeps it upright, 1 is as worked out, higher exaggerates, negative tilts the other way.

Whether the wearer's arm on the attachment side is automatically aimed at the carried entity (both arms for a centred attachment). Turn off to animate the arms yourself with the argon.carry_* queries.
Whether the released entity takes no fall damage from its next fall.

name: State Selector
description: On activation, changes a block state property (e.g. "open", "lit", "facing") of the block you target, using "block_properties". With several entries, a held key scrolls a menu of those that apply.

fields.description: The maximum distance, in blocks, the raycast can reach.
Optional whitelist of blocks (explicit IDs and/or tags) this ability can affect; if unset, any block is eligible.

One or more property definitions to offer; each has "property" (the BlockState property name, e.g. "open"/"facing"/"waterlogged" - not a hardcoded list, whatever the block actually has is used), "operation" (SET/NEXT/PREVIOUS/TOGGLE), an optional "value" (used by SET, given in its normal string form e.g. "true"/"east"/"3"), and an optional "allowed_values" string list restricting and ordering which values that entry may ever use. A single entry (or a bare object instead of a list) applies immediately; multiple entries open the scrollable picker described above.
If false (default), refuses to touch any block that has a block entity (chests, furnaces, etc.) as a safety measure.
If true (default), the change triggers normal neighbor updates (redstone, shape updates, etc.); the client is always synced regardless.
If true (default), the resulting state must be able to survive at that position or the change is cancelled.

If false (default), refuses to change a small set of known structural, multi-position properties ("half", "part" - e.g. doors, beds, tall plants) since changing only one half can desync the pair. This check is not exhaustive for modded blocks with different structural property names; use "block_filter" to scope those explicitly.

The blip color used for hostile mobs.
The blip color used for non-hostile mobs.

name: Tentacle Guard
description: While enabled, wraps idle appendages around the torso to absorb damage from within "block_angle" of your facing, up to "guard_threshold". Beyond that the guard breaks, hurting you and disabling blocking for "break_lockout" ticks.

fields.description: How many appendages must stay wrapped for guard to actually absorb damage; below this, hits go through normally.
How many appendages this ability claims and wraps at once.
Cumulative damage the guard can absorb before it breaks.
Self-damage dealt to the wearer when the guard breaks.
Ticks after breaking before guard can absorb damage again.

The cone, in degrees centered on the wearer's facing, that incoming damage must arrive within to be blockable - also how widely the wrapped appendages themselves spread around the body. 180 (default) blocks (and wraps) anything in front; 360 blocks (and wraps) from any direction.
Knockback velocity applied to the attacker on a successful block.

description: While enabled, scales the tick speed of entities, crops, and redstone per the affect_* settings according to "speed", affecting players only if TIME_CONTROL_CAN_AFFECT_PLAYERS is enabled.

Whether entity movement/AI within range is slowed, sped up, or stopped.

Whether scheduled block ticks and block entities (furnaces, hoppers, pistons, redstone) are frozen world-wide, but only when speed is exactly 0.

name: Beam
description: Shoots a beam in the direction the player is looking at.

fields.description: The id of the beam renderer to use
The damage the beam deals to entities
The damage type used when an entity is hit. If not set, it counts as a normal player or mob attack.
The maximum distance the beam can travel

If the beam should cause fire on blocks. Claim protection, spawn protection and the mobGriefing gamerule (for non-players) are respected
If the beam should smelt hit blocks. Claim protection, spawn protection and the mobGriefing gamerule (for non-players) are respected

Action(s) that are performed every tick the beam hits a block. They run for the entity that shoots the beam, but commands and sounds are positioned where the beam hits, and the hit block is used as the block position.

name: Team Formation
description: On activation, opens a client-side GUI to name a team and invite up to 6 online players by username, each receiving a clickable chat message that adds them to the team on acceptance.

name: Mode Switch
description: Switches between a map of modes. By default it cycles to the next mode whose conditions are met each time it is activated. With the menu selection, holding the ability's key opens a row of all available modes next to the ability in the ability bar instead. Scroll to pick one, then let go of the key (or click, see "confirm") to switch to it. The menu works with every key behaviour, but "held" is recommended, since the ability then also counts as enabled while the menu is open.

fields.description: A map of mode key -> mode (at least one). Each mode has a required "title", an optional "icon" texture, and optional "conditions" (a mode is only switchable-to while its conditions are met, and it is hidden from the menu otherwise). "on_selected" and "on_unselected" are optional actions, run on the server when the mode becomes the active one or stops being it. They only run on an actual change, so the first mode, which is active from the start, doesn't run "on_selected" until it is switched back to. The key is the unique id used by the mode condition and value.

How a mode is picked. "cycle" switches to the next mode on every activation, "menu" opens a selection menu while the key is held. The menu needs a key that can be held, so it does not work with scroll or GUI button key binds.

Only used by the menu. "release" switches to the picked mode when the key is let go. "left_click" and "right_click" switch when clicking while the menu is open, and letting go of the key without clicking closes the menu without changing anything.
If the new mode is briefly shown in the middle of the screen after switching.

name: Slowfall
description: Makes the entity fall slower.

name: Screen Shake
description: Shakes the camera of the player who has the ability while it is enabled. The strength follows the ability's animation timer, so setting an "animation_timer" in the properties makes the shake fade in and out smoothly. Without one, the shake starts and stops instantly.

fields.description: How far the camera moves, in degrees. A single number shakes yaw and pitch by that amount, an object sets yaw, pitch and roll separately.
How many shake cycles happen per tick. Higher values shake faster. Can be a dynamic value, the shake then speeds up or slows down smoothly.

name: Danger Sense
description: While enabled, detects hostile mobs (and neutral ones targeting you) within "hostile_range" and players who recently damaged you. Optionally lights the screen border toward each danger.

fields.description: How far out to search for hostile/aggressive mobs, evaluated fresh every scan. Also doubles as the glow's fade-in distance: a detected danger's glow eases from invisible at this range up to full strength the closer it gets, rather than snapping on the instant it's detected.
How long after being damaged a player who dealt that damage still counts as a detected danger.
Entities holding any of these powers never trigger danger sense, whether they're a nearby hostile mob or a recent attacker.
If true, lights up the screen's border in the direction of each detected danger.
The color of the screen-border glow, when "show_visual" is true.
The glow's peak opacity at its brightest point, from 0 (invisible) to 1 (fully opaque).
How far the glow reaches inward from the screen's edge, in pixels.
How far, in pixels measured along the screen's border, the glow extends from its brightest point before fully fading out.

Spawn offset in front of the entity (negative = behind), relative to its facing direction.

name: Tentacle Strike
description: Sends one idle appendage to strike a target within "attack_range", dealing damage on impact before retracting. "attack_pattern": "direct_strike" aims at what you look at, "auto_nearest" at the nearest target.

Knockback velocity applied to the target on impact.

"direct_strike" (a random idle appendage strikes whatever the wearer looks at, once per activation) or "auto_nearest" (continuously, whichever idle appendage is nearest strikes the nearest target in range).
